response.query: Which sensitivity analyses (leave-one-source-out, temporal splits, cluster-parameter sweeps, source-weight perturbation) are essential to test robustness of document-level governance proxies?
response.answer: Leave-one-source-out, temporal splits, and source-weight perturbation are essential for testing robustness of document-level governance proxies. Cluster-parameter sweeps are also important for assessing variability in governance metrics.

results.title: Automated machine learning: past, present and future
results.content: J Mach Learn Res 20(1):1997–2017")), we focus our discussion on three key components found in all AutoML systems: (1) the _search space_ that incorporates all design choices in a given machine-learning pipeline (i.e., all algorithms in a pipeline, their hyperparameters, or architectural hyperparameters of a neural network; (2) the _search strategy_ used to find good candidate solutions within the search space, i.e., performance-optimising instantiations of the design choices; and (3) the _performance evaluation (or estimation) technique_ used to automatically assess the performance of candidate solutions on a fraction of a given dataset. Following this background material, we present three categories of AutoML approaches: hyperparameter optimisation techniques, which assume that the only design choices to be made are hyperparameters of a given machine-learning pipeline or system; NAS techniques, which focus on design choices related to the architecture of deep neural networks; and broad-spectrum AutoML systems that consider design spaces containing broad classes of machine-learning algorithms, but are not specifically focused on deep neural networks.
